platform_editions.programmatic_file_access: Standalone Pulse retains exclusive offline read/edit/write access to supported document versions. Embedded Pulse 3.0 uses the Abacus-owned document API; never opens a second file writer. Preserve formulas and invalidate dependent cached results.
platform_editions.positioning: Integrated spreadsheet, structured-data analysis and reporting environment, programmable in Pulse. The November 1980 release serves contemporary business workflows; direct competition with the historical 1983 Lotus 1-2-3 belongs to a later Abacus version.

reporting.continuity: Extend Abacus 2.0 report/document layouts, spreadsheet fields and one-off/repeating sections.
reporting.presentation: Retain standard TUI editing/navigation; add capability-aware graphical preview with titles, axes and legends. Support monochrome patterns and available display modes through the display API.
reporting.output: Print reports and charts through supported printer drivers; define pagination and refresh stale query/formula results before output.
reporting.sources: Worksheet ranges, formatted tables and grouped query results; keep source references stable after sorting and filtering.

data_interchange.bpi_continuity: Retain versioned BPI summary imports as independent planning inputs with reconciliation and decimal validation; no ledger write-back or live database connection.
data_interchange.csv: Schema-mapped CSV import with quoted fields, delimiter/character encoding selection, explicit date and decimal conventions, null handling, text preservation for identifiers and rejected-record diagnostics. Provide value-only CSV export with explicit loss-of-formulas/types warning.
data_interchange.vsam: Import host-exported sequential logical records from supported VSAM datasets using a supplied field/record layout. Host-side export (for example IDCAMS REPRO) and a documented transfer path are prerequisites; raw VSAM clusters, indexes and disk images are not desktop interchange formats.
data_interchange.vsam_conversion: Declare supported record boundaries, lengths, offsets, keys and character encoding; convert EBCDIC, supported binary, packed-decimal and zoned-decimal fields explicitly. Reject unsupported layouts without silently changing values.
data_interchange.migration: Versioned document format; preserve supported older worksheets and reports. Older Abacus/Pulse editions must reject unsupported new features before writing. Explicit value-only export is a lossy interchange option.

release_scope.status: Author-approved offering requirements; implementation and measured qualification remain pending.
release_scope.launch: Flat typed formatted tables, bounded columnar processing, virtual columns, unique-key lookups, a documented read-only SQL subset, graphical reports, embedded Pulse and mapped imports.
later_milestones: Bounded nested arrays, maps and structs with explicit expansion/indexing and aggregation semantics; format extension points reserved in 3.0.
Broader query capabilities and competitive response to Lotus 1-2-3 in a later Abacus version.
release_scope.later_version_and_date: Not assigned; no later feature is represented as available at the 1980 launch.
release_scope.resource_policy: Qualify real Artemis 128/256 KiB configurations and later Artemis PRO separately. Record application/OS memory, storage, dataset size and timings; larger jobs may require expansion or disk-backed execution. No new minimum RAM or maximum row count is asserted.
release_scope.acceptance_workflow: Import sales records, join customer/product information, calculate margins, group by region, print a graphical report, save/reopen, then repeat using a Pulse script.
acceptance_requirements: Measure memory, disk I/O, import/query/recalculation/report times and compression on named datasets.
Verify import conversion/rejections, decimal rounding, nulls, duplicate lookup keys and join cardinality.
Verify cancellation, grouped undo, edit visibility, dependency invalidation, save recovery and unsupported-version rejection.

platform_editions.product_status: Accepted 1983 planning baseline; implementation, memory fit and release qualification pending.
platform_editions.description: ROM-backed successor to AIONix: protected preemptive multitasking, documented ERA ABI compatibility, recoverable HDD storage, user access management and an event-driven TUI designed for later graphical windowing.
platform_editions.delivery: At least 256 KiB directly executable shared OS ROM, alongside at least 256 KiB DRAM. EEPROM BIOS remains boot/diagnostic firmware. Optional services, larger utilities and patches load from disk; do not copy the entire OS ROM into RAM.

rom_execution.mapping: Shared read-only executable mappings; private writable data per process. Cacheable ROM with independently qualified timing.
rom_execution.updates: Versioned dispatch tables and page-sized RAM patch overlays; ROM version/checksum checks and recovery boot bypassing disk patches. Patched pages consume DRAM.
rom_execution.physical_implementation: 256 KiB minimum system ROM bank; chip organization, package count, board mounting and timing remain qualification decisions.

compatibility.scope: Documented ERA AIONix user binaries, instruction semantics and C ABI; not Z80 binary compatibility.
compatibility.mechanism: Executable ABI version selects legacy adapters; stable library dispatch and capability discovery.
compatibility.limits: Undocumented kernel dependencies, privileged drivers and direct hardware access require separate qualification; portable Z80 C applications require recompilation.

multitasking.kernel: Compact monolithic kernel; timer-preempted user processes, bounded non-preemptible kernel critical sections.
requirements: Checked user pointers and protected kernel/device mappings
Process-exit cleanup of files, memory, locks and child state
Per-process memory, file and request limits
Short interrupt handlers with deferred work
Kernel-controlled DMA with checked pinned buffers
multitasking.limits: Process isolation does not isolate kernel/driver faults or independently constrain DMA. Fully preemptible kernel and application threads are not initial requirements.

posix_direction.reference: POSIX.1-2024 / Issue 8, used as an out-of-world future-informed design reference, not a 1983 certification claim.
initial_target: Consistent open/read/write/close/lseek/stat and descriptor duplication, inheritance and errors
Reliable existing copy-on-write fork, exec, wait, exit status and environment
Defined signal delivery, masks, dispositions and interrupted-call semantics
Canonical/raw terminal modes, terminal attributes and foreground process groups
Hierarchical paths, working directories, hard links and symbolic links
Pipes with EOF/broken-pipe semantics and readiness multiplexing
Shell quoting, redirection, pipelines, variables and exit statuses
Wall clock, monotonic elapsed time and explicit timestamp formats
later: Efficient spawn without replacing fork semantics
Broader file control and memory mapping
Broader utilities, locales, threads and timers
posix_direction.conformance: Publish per-interface implemented/partial/absent matrix and unsupported-operation errors; names alone do not establish conformance.

filesystem.design: Versioned inode-based filesystem; directory entries separate from metadata.
filesystem.qualification_note: Testing range, not capacity ceiling or a change to bundled HDD sizes.
requirements: Ownership, permissions, link counts and timestamps
Mount support and logical-sector driver interface with CHS translation when required
Clean/dirty volume state and consistency checker
Ordered metadata writes and explicit synchronization
Backup/restore utilities and defined durable-save ordering
filesystem.later: Small metadata journal after write-order and power-loss testing; journal does not by itself guarantee application-data durability.

initial_target: Numeric users and groups
Owner/group/other read/write/execute and directory search permissions
Creation masks
Real/effective credentials
Login sessions and home directories
Protected password database with salted costed hashing selected against CPU budget
Administrative control of devices, mounts and configuration
Kernel enforcement on all relevant operations
Protected administrative audit records
user_access.privilege: Qualify credential and exec transitions before enabling set-user-ID programs. Server authenticates identity rather than trusting client-supplied UID.
user_access.later: Extended ACLs and more elaborate policies.

ui_layers.name: Application layer
ui_layers.responsibility: Business logic and semantic commands such as Open, Save, Select and Cancel, independent of rendering.

ui_layers.name: Abstraction layer
ui_layers.responsibility: Events, menus, forms, lists, focus, layout, text measurement and drawing contexts.

ui_layers.name: Translation and compatibility layer
ui_layers.responsibility: Existing TUI adapters, terminal rendering, device backends and legacy ABI behavior; later graphical renderers.

ui_layers.name: OS native API
ui_layers.responsibility: Processes, files, IPC, timers, input devices and controlled display access.

ui_contract.implementation: Logical layers primarily in shared libraries plus a small UI service; not four mandatory processes or IPC crossings. Extend the existing portable C API.
initial_target: Unified bounded event queue for keys, timers, focus, redraw and future pointer events
Semantic commands separated from physical keys
Opaque window/view handles initially representing text regions
Clipping, invalidation and repaint requests
Layout constraints and explicit text measurement
Separate cell and pixel coordinates
Bounded clipboard and selection ownership
Capability/version discovery for graphics, fonts, color and pointer input
ui_contract.memory: Compact text state, dirty regions and redraw callbacks; no mandatory full-screen RAM backing bitmap.
ui_contract.next_generation: Windowed GUI; legacy character applications run in terminal windows. Adapters do not automatically redesign old UIs.

memory_management.initial: Shared ROM code, sparse page tables, small kernel stacks, reliable copy-on-write and graceful allocation failure.
memory_management.later: Controlled disk-backed paging/swap only after restart, locking and I/O qualification; keep fault handlers and essential paging state resident.
memory_management.policy: Swap handles occasional pressure, not a routinely oversized working set; ROM does not replace writable RAM.

qualification: Measured ROM/RAM footprint and Abacus/compiler/server workloads
TUI capability fallback and legacy terminal behavior

priority_assessment.feasibility: Strong existing foundation; fit and patch behavior must be measured.
Feasible with ERA protection and restart rules; extensive verification.
20–100 MB addressing is straightforward; crash recovery is the main risk.
Phase interfaces; full contemporary conformance excluded.
Depends on proven faults and I/O; not initial release gate.
Not required in the minimum 1983 configuration.

release_scope.initial: ROM execution, documented legacy ABI, protected preemptive processes, recoverable HDD storage, users/permissions, POSIX-oriented subset and event-driven TUI groundwork.
release_scope.later: Paging/swap, metadata journal, broader networking/threads/locales and full windowed GUI.
release_scope.schedule: Retain planned NCC announcement; no new shipment date or completed implementation claimed.

resource_planning.basis: Engineering allocation target, not a measured fit or maximum. Server retains its existing 1 MiB configuration.

platform_editions.development_lineage: Joint DRI founded in late 1974; earlier documented hardware abstraction. September 1976 is the Aurelia implementation agreement. Alternate 1.4-derived core retains ordinary CP/M interfaces; Platform Extensions 1.0 are an optional, versioned layer, not features claimed for historical CP/M 1.4.
platform_editions.description: A ROM-adapted CP/M 1.4 platform combining the standard application and file-service interfaces with Logix memory, peripheral and TUI services. The same architecture supports Aurelia and Aurelia+.

vanilla_architecture.execution_model: Single user, one foreground application; conventional operating-system and application images execute in RAM.

memory_layout.purpose: System vectors, default file-control information and command/disk buffer
Transient Program Area (TPA): application code and data
CCP, then BDOS, then machine-specific BIOS at the high end of configured memory

components.name: CCP — Console Command Processor
components.description: Reads commands, executes built-in commands and loads transient programs. Uses BDOS services.

components.name: BDOS — Basic Disk Operating System
components.description: Provides console and file services, directory/allocation management and record operations. Calls BIOS for hardware operations.

components.name: BIOS — Basic Input/Output System
components.description: Machine-specific console, printer and disk primitives, including startup and sector transfers.

components.name: TPA — Transient Program Area
components.description: Application code and data in RAM. A memory region, not an executable OS module.

components.name: Transient utilities
components.description: Separate editing, copying, assembly, debugging and maintenance programs loaded when needed.

changes_from_1_3: Four logical disk drives; BIOS drive selection accepts 0–3.
Drive selection can maintain additional disk state.
BDOS begins one 256-byte page lower; CCP and BIOS bases remain unchanged.
DE returns the same value as HL.
BDOS implementation is divided into a PL/M main body and an assembly interface module.
limits: No built-in banked-ROM runtime, cartridge manager or dynamic driver registry.
No shared TUI widgets, clipboard or resident Business Tools workspace.
The generalized CP/M 2.0 disk-parameter-block model is not part of vanilla 1.4.

internal_organization.name: Boot and recovery firmware
internal_organization.description: Initialize hardware, discover the system cartridge and provide diagnostics/recovery.

internal_organization.name: Memory / cartridge runtime
internal_organization.residence: Stable common-memory entry routines plus ROM services
internal_organization.description: Select banks, preserve mappings and stacks, support nested calls and execute cartridge components.

internal_organization.name: Hardware drivers and device registry
internal_organization.residence: Motherboard ROM, device ROM and replaceable extensions
internal_organization.description: Operate video, keyboard, floppy and FlexiBUS hardware; discover devices and register compatible drivers.

internal_organization.name: CP/M BIOS adapter
internal_organization.residence: Stable firmware primitives plus system-cartridge adaptation
internal_organization.description: Translate CP/M console, printer and disk operations into Logix driver calls.

internal_organization.name: CP/M 1.4-derived BDOS
internal_organization.residence: System cartridge; mutable state in RAM
internal_organization.description: Preserve file/application services; adapt disk-format assumptions and code for banked ROM execution.

internal_organization.name: CP/M 1.4-derived CCP
internal_organization.residence: System cartridge; command buffers in RAM
internal_organization.description: Interpret commands, launch disk/cartridge applications and use shared command-line editing.

internal_organization.name: Logix TUI and shared services
internal_organization.residence: CP/M system cartridge; mutable state in reserved RAM; hardware operations delegated to drivers
internal_organization.description: Own the shared application-facing screen and keyboard API, editing controls, menus, forms, lists, popup windows, clipboard service and workspace entry/return support. Business Tools and other compatible applications call these services rather than carrying a second shared TUI library.

internal_organization.name: Utilities and applications
internal_organization.description: Use standard CP/M calls and, when Logix-aware, the versioned extension interface.

logix_requirements: Preserve standard CP/M entry points, loading conventions and available-memory boundaries.
Adapt both BIOS and relevant BDOS assumptions to Aurelia floppy formats.
Keep bank-switching entry code, stack and critical interrupt handling permanently accessible.
Separate ROM code/constants from RAM state; adapt self-modifying routines.
Discover cartridge/device ROMs through defined, versioned interfaces.
Map Logix peripherals to standard CP/M console, printer and disk services.
Provide a separate versioned Logix service interface and C bindings.
Drivers use bounded DMA transfers with physical-bank descriptors and device-ready handshakes; abort/drain transfers before warm boot or reusing buffers.
Video API exposes dedicated sprite SRAM, atomic descriptor swaps and upload-port backpressure; use programmed I/O fallback where peripherals lack DMA endpoints.

tui_features.name: Layout and screen
tui_features.description: Query usable dimensions, clip and scroll; separate document coordinates from screen coordinates.

tui_features.name: Adaptive layouts
tui_features.description: Compact 40-column and expanded 80-column layouts; dialogs, long names and errors fit either width.

tui_features.name: Semantic colors
tui_features.description: Normal text, selection and warning roles map to color or monochrome attributes.

tui_features.name: Input
tui_features.description: Structured character, function/navigation key and modifier events; blocking input and polling.

tui_features.name: Controls
tui_features.description: Fields, lists, menus, dialogs, popup windows and consistent focus movement.

tui_features.name: Editing

tui_features.name: Clipboard
tui_features.description: Explicit formats, lengths, bounded capacity, ownership and errors.

tui_features.name: Context lifecycle

tui_features.name: Timing

compatibility_notes: Ordinary CP/M applications keep character/file services; rich TUI behavior requires use of Logix APIs.
Shared TUI routines do not require multitasking; applications may remain sequential.
Clipboard capacity, exact widgets and workspace behavior remain implementation decisions.
Keep the same API behavior across Aurelia, Aurelia+ and Artemis.
Do not assume display stride, video RAM address, last column or direct peripheral registers.

Artemis implementation mediates process access to shared clipboard and display services.

tui_ownership.boundary: System services supply reusable controls and clipboard/workspace mechanisms. Applications own their documents, calculations, file-management workflows and calendar records.

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation conformance and measured performance remain to be validated.
implementation_design.title: BPI transactional client/server v1
implementation_design.architecture: Thin Z80/ERA clients send bounded business operations to an Artemis PRO server. Query evaluation, indexes, validation, accounting posting and transactions execute on the server; clients do not fetch arbitrary database pages.

transactions.concurrency: Single serialized writer for v1 with short transactions and bounded reader locks; no long interactive transaction while a user edits a form.
transactions.commit: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.
transactions.recovery: On startup validate checksums and recover committed log records; incomplete transactions never become visible. Use shadow page/index replacement or another explicitly validated torn-write-safe method.
transactions.failure: Do not claim durable commit until disk/controller completion semantics are proven; no battery-backed cache is assumed.
transactions.log_format: Redo-only changed-record/page after-images with transaction ID, sequence, length and checksum; the commit marker covers transaction record count and checksum. Persist duplicate-suppression outcomes in the same transaction.
transactions.buffer_policy: Do not write uncommitted changes to database files (no-steal); cap transaction size to available transaction buffers.
transactions.checkpoint: Write replacement pages and indexes to new locations, force them, then alternate checksummed generation-numbered root/checkpoint records. Retain the preceding valid root and necessary redo log until the new checkpoint is durable.

protocol.transport: Length-framed requests over TCP; bounded messages and chunked results.
protocol.duplicate_suppression: Store committed write request IDs and outcomes durably. After reconnect, clients query status or retry with the same ID; never post the same payment twice.

data_integrity: Amounts use explicitly scaled integers/decimal rules, never unspecified binary floating-point rounding.
Record currency, rounding, posting dates, account periods and unique document IDs.
Cross-module posting is atomic and produces an append-only audit record.
operations: Role-based authorization and server-side input validation
Backup captures a consistent checkpoint plus required logs; test restoration onto a clean disk.
Bounded log growth, disk-full handling and operator-visible recovery status
Plan backups and report traffic around the negotiated shared 100/250/500/1000 kbit/s raw LAN budget and measured payload throughput; slower admitted hosts limit the whole network.

initial_limits.status: Specified acceptance target, not measured capacity.
initial_limits.client_policy: Bounded pages of results and forms; no entire-table download or whole-document duplication.

acceptance_tests: Full disk, corrupt log tail and failed backup restore

subcomponents.name: Disk browser

subcomponents.name: Calculator

subcomponents.name: Calendar / scheduler

runtime_notes: The cartridge remains a 16 KB product capacity; removing duplicate routines does not establish a measured free-space budget.
Uses one cartridge slot alongside the CP/M system cartridge.
Code executes from banked ROM where practical; writable application state is held in RAM.
Reusable TUI widgets, screen and input primitives, clipboard ownership and workspace mechanisms belong to the CP/M system cartridge.
Application-specific text editing, file browsing, calculation and scheduling logic remain in this cartridge.
The applications call the system TUI interface; they do not require their own copy of its library.
A resident workspace reserves RAM explicitly; the cartridge does not imply multitasking.

compatibility_policy.eligibility: Any manufacturer or independent integrator may implement the published environment without a bespoke partnership or mandatory certification.
compatibility_policy.binary: Existing Z80 binaries require compatible instruction execution and the specified OS/runtime and memory behaviour; CP/M alone is insufficient. Other processors need an appropriate port or execution solution.
compatibility_policy.hardware: Native video, keyboards, disks and printers may be exposed through adapters. FlexiBUS and Logix video hardware are separate optional profiles. Full hardware clones may implement those published interfaces under their applicable terms.
compatibility_policy.applications: Named supported platforms are tested configurations, not an exclusive permission list. Independently implemented environments may run properly licensed applications; certification identifies precisely what AION tested.
compatibility_policy.scope: Released 8-bit Aurelia interfaces only. No future processor names, word size, ISA, binaries or architectural details before NCC 1980.
compatibility_policy.licensing: Specification and self-test requirements are freely accessible. Kit fee covers media, manuals and updates supplied with the kit. Reference runtime adapters may be modified and redistributed without per-machine royalty under standard terms. No automatic licence to redistribute CP/M, application binaries, firmware or trademarks; obtain each required licence separately. Proprietary application source is not included.
compatibility_policy.delivery: Printed manuals/source listings and disks; host/media conversion quoted separately.
compatibility_policy.certification: Optional, configuration- and version-specific. Manufacturer-declared compatibility is distinct from AION-tested application compatibility. FlexiBUS electrical/protocol and Logix display tests are separate claims.

platform_editions.description: One Artemis PRO server entitlement and four concurrent network developer sessions. Hardware, network adapters, hub and backup media sold separately. C IDE version 2 runs locally after network loading; shared source/results live on the server.
features: AIONix Server November 1981 services: users, groups, authentication, project permissions, home directories, quotas and administration
Repository: atomic multi-file commits, author/date/message, branches, release labels, diffs, rollback and comments tied to immutable revisions; isolated workspaces, saving is not committing
Collaboration: text channels, posts and replies with file/revision/commit references; shared calendar, meetings, invitations, tasks, owners, deadlines and milestones
C Development Environment 2: local Artemis ERA/Z80 builds; compact Aurelia/Aurelia+ TUI and local Z80 tools; queued server ERA/heavy builds
Initial targets CP/M/Z80 and AIONix/ERA with separate binaries, startup code and libraries; Breakthru TUI portability layer and target adapters
Reproducible builds record source revisions, compiler versions, build settings and target libraries
Network loader uses bounded transfers; acknowledged saves and recoverable workspaces after disconnect
Apple and Commodore target packages are future roadmap work; no launch support or binary compatibility claim

specification.server: Artemis PRO, recommended 1 MiB; existing 5 MB disk supports bounded pilot projects only. Archive old history and rotate external floppy backups; larger qualified storage required for substantial projects and is not bundled or priced here.
specification.clients: Artemis, Aurelia and Aurelia+ with network upgrade; Aurelia compact tools use sequential overlays within its CP/M memory profile. No full suite resident in 48 KiB claim.
specification.qualification: Four concurrent developers is a validation target, not measured throughput. Gate release on commit recovery, access control, backup/restore, conflict handling and both target regression suites.

commercial_unit.unit: one server, four concurrent developer sessions
commercial_unit.renewal: No automatic paid renewal assumed; first-year support capped at 12 staff-hours. Further work quoted separately.
commercial_unit.expansion: Additional concurrency packs planned, not priced or counted as shipping offers.

delivery_cost_assumptions.note: One combined package; do not add its client/server editions or old IDE/SDK to its cost. Development/NRE excluded from unit cost.

specification.sponsored_deployment: Autodesk whole-team deployment from late January 1982: team_development_program.json/autodesk_sponsored_deployment. Sponsor supplies hardware, qualified concurrency/storage and dedicated support beyond retail caps; retail entitlement remains unchanged.

adoption_pricing.reference_basis: Pre-change June 15 1982 Team Edition retail, previously used as the explicit November 1981 launch-price proxy. Not a historical market quotation.
